adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:338 — strategy.close() (called by arroyo on every partition revocation) shuts down the factory-wide shared FixedQueuePool, so after the first rebalance the next strategy's queue.put raises ShutDown, submit()'s broad except (line 317-325) marks the offset complete, and every later uptime result is silently dropped but committed; no test does close+recreate, so this passes CI

adjudication.rationale: In `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, `self.queue_pool` is created once (factory-wide) for mode `thread-queue-parallel` and then reused in every `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` call (`queue_pool=self.queue_pool`). However `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` unconditionally calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which calls `q.shutdown()` on each underlying `queue.Queue`. After that, future `FixedQueuePool.submit()` calls will attempt `work_queue.put(work_item)` on a shut down queue (raising `queue.ShutDown`), which is caught by the broad `except Exception` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` and results in `add_offset`+`complete_offset` without processing—making the message eligible for commit in `_commit_loop` (data loss with committed offsets). The diff contains no logic to recreate `queue_pool` after a strategy closes, and tests don’t cover close+recreate, so this failure mode would not be detected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:278 — OffsetTracker lives on the shared pool and is never cleared per assignment, so a revoked partition with committable offsets (e.g. items finished after the final commit pass in close()) stays in get_committable_offsets; arroyo stage_offsets raises "cannot stage offsets for unassigned partitions" on the whole dict, mark_committed never runs, and commits stall for every partition, forever

adjudication.rationale: In the new thread-queue-parallel mode, `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single long-lived `FixedQueuePool` (and thus a single `OffsetTracker`) stored on the factory (`self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)`). `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` always calls `committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()` and passes the whole dict to `commit_function` without any filtering/clearing by the currently-assigned partitions, and there is no API to drop partitions from `OffsetTracker` when partitions are revoked. If `commit_function`/`commit` rejects offsets for unassigned partitions (plausible in Arroyo), the exception path logs and retries forever (`except Exception: logger.exception("Error in commit loop")`), and because `mark_committed` is only called after a successful commit, the stale partition remains committable and can block committing offsets for all partitions indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:185 — queue.Queue() is unbounded and submit() never raises MessageRejected, so contrary to the docstring's claimed "natural backpressure", a slow or hung result_processor (a poison group) makes arroyo keep consuming into memory while the partition's contiguous commit point stays pinned (no timeout); this ends in OOM plus a large replay

adjudication.rationale: In FixedQueuePool.__init__ the work queues are created with `queue.Queue()` (default `maxsize=0`, i.e. unbounded). In FixedQueuePool.submit and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit, items are enqueued via `work_queue.put(work_item)` with no maxsize/timeout and there is no mechanism to raise backpressure (e.g., MessageRejected) to stop Arroyo from continuing to consume. If `result_processor` is slow/hung for a group, queued WorkItems can accumulate indefinitely in memory, while OffsetTracker will keep offsets outstanding and prevent commits past the pinned offset, leading to large in-memory growth and replay on restart. This contradicts the docstring claim of “Natural backpressure when queues fill up” and represents a real failure mode introduced by the new strategy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:287 — commit() (arroyo StreamProcessor.__commit -> KafkaConsumer.stage_offsets/commit_offsets) is called from a background thread concurrently with the consumer thread's poll and rebalance callbacks, which mutate the same unsynchronized __offsets/__staged_offsets/commit-policy state; arroyo's Commit contract assumes the processing thread

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a background `commit_thread` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__` that calls `self.commit_function(committable)` inside `_commit_loop` (queue_consumer.py), and `commit_function` is wired to the Arroyo `commit` callback in `ResultsStrategyFactory.create_thread_queue_parallel_worker`. So commits are invoked off the processing thread. However, the finding’s stronger claim about Arroyo’s internal `__offsets/__staged_offsets` being unsynchronized and the Commit contract requiring the processing thread is not verifiable from this diff alone (it depends on Arroyo internals/contract not shown here). This is still a concrete, diff-grounded concurrency/architecture concern created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:281 — The offsets_committed metric is emitted before commit_function runs, and commit failures are only logged inside the thread (poll() never surfaces them), so the health signal stays green while commits are permanently failing

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop`, the code increments `metrics.incr("remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed", ...)` before calling `self.commit_function(committable)`. If `commit_function` raises, the exception is swallowed by the surrounding `try/except` and only logged (`logger.exception("Error in commit loop")`), and `poll()` only reports queue depth/total queued—there is no surfaced failure signal. This is not a functional correctness defect in offset tracking (since `mark_committed` is only done after a successful commit call), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/health-signal issue: the metric named "offsets_committed" can be emitted even when commits are failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:234 — shutdown() sets worker.shutdown=True before q.shutdown(immediate=False), so workers exit after their current item instead of draining; close() also stops the commit thread before the pool, so work completed after the final commit pass is never committed; both cause duplicate reprocessing on every rebalance

adjudication.rationale: In FixedQueuePool.shutdown(), the code sets worker.shutdown = True before shutting down the queues. Since OrderedQueueWorker.run() loops `while not self.shutdown`, a worker will stop after finishing its current item and will not drain remaining queued WorkItems, leaving their offsets in OffsetTracker.outstanding forever. Separately, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() stops and joins the commit thread before shutting down the queue pool, so any offsets completed by workers after the last commit-loop iteration (or during shutdown) will not be committed. Both behaviors are directly visible in the diff and can lead to reprocessing/duplicates after restart/rebalance due to uncommitted offsets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:89 — The contiguous-offset scan requires every integer offset to be seen, so any legitimate Kafka offset gap (transaction control markers, compaction) permanently blocks commits for that partition while all_offsets grows without bound

adjudication.rationale: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets`, the contiguous scan iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1)` and breaks unless `offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding`. Since `all_offsets` only contains offsets that were actually submitted via `add_offset`, any observed gap (i.e., consumer sees offsets 100, 102, 103 and never sees 101) will cause the loop to break at the missing integer and prevent committing beyond it, even if later offsets are fully processed. While stuck, `add_offset` continues accumulating higher offsets in `self.all_offsets[partition]`, and because `mark_committed` never advances, that set can grow without being pruned. adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1922 — The error-handling test asserts nothing was committed, but the worker's finally marks failed offsets complete, so 102 will be committed; it only passes because the 1s commit tick hasn't fired yet (timing-dependent, and it asserts the opposite of real behavior)

In `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` (added in this diff), two messages (offsets 100, 101) are submitted and the first processing call raises; nevertheless both offsets will be completed, so the commit loop can commit the highest contiguous processed offset (101), and `commit_offsets` will pass `101 + 1 = 102` to the commit callback. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:142 — queue.ShutDown/Queue.shutdown only exist on Python 3.13+; on older runtimes, any exception escaping result_processor makes evaluating `except queue.ShutDown` raise AttributeError, which kills the worker thread and stalls its queue and partition commits forever, and pool shutdown can't wake workers blocked in get()

adjudication.rationale: The new implementation in `queue_consumer.py` relies on `queue.ShutDown` (e.g., `except queue.ShutDown:` in `OrderedQueueWorker.run`) and `Queue.shutdown()` (in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown`). Those APIs are not present in Python versions prior to 3.13. If `queue.ShutDown` is missing, then when an exception is raised in the `try` body, evaluating `except queue.ShutDown` will itself raise `AttributeError`, killing the worker thread. Likewise, if `Queue.shutdown` is missing, `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` cannot wake worker threads blocked on `work_queue.get()` (no timeout/sentinel is used), so shutdown/join can hang and offset commits can stall.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:338 — Strategy close() shuts down the factory-owned FixedQueuePool, but create_with_partitions (result_consumer.py:254) reuses that dead pool after a rebalance, so every later put() raises queue.ShutDown and no workers exist to process messages

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates and stores a single `FixedQueuePool` on the factory instance when `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` (result_consumer.py: `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)`). `create_with_partitions` then reuses that same `self.queue_pool` for each new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` (create_thread_queue_parallel_worker asserts `self.queue_pool is not None` and passes it through). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:317 — Any exception in submit (e.g. queue.ShutDown from put on the shut-down pool, or a grouping_fn error) marks the offset completed, so the commit loop commits messages that were never processed (silent data loss)

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, the broad `except Exception` handler logs and then unconditionally calls `add_offset(...)` and `complete_offset(...)` for the message when `message.value` is a `BrokerValue`. This means failures before enqueueing/processing (e.g., `grouping_fn(result)` raising, or `FixedQueuePool.submit` raising due to `work_queue.put(...)` failing on a shut down queue) will still mark the offset as processed. The commit loop (`_commit_loop`) uses `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets()` and will commit these offsets even though `result_processor` was never invoked for that message, causing silent message loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:90 — Contiguity scan requires every integer offset to be in all_offsets, so any Kafka offset gap (transaction markers, compaction) permanently stalls commits for that partition and all_offsets grows without bound

adjudication.rationale: In OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets, the contiguity check iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1)` and breaks if `offset not in all_offsets` (or is outstanding). Since `all_offsets` only contains offsets actually observed via add_offset (i.e., delivered messages), any Kafka gap (e.g., skipped control records/aborted transaction markers) means some integers in that range will never be in `all_offsets`, causing the loop to break and preventing commits from advancing past the first gap. If commits stall, `all_offsets[partition]` also cannot be trimmed by mark_committed, so it can grow unbounded for that partition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:74 — OffsetTracker never drops state for revoked partitions, so a tracker shared across strategies would keep sending unassigned partitions to commit(), which raises and blocks the whole batch every tick

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates and retains a single `FixedQueuePool` (and its `OffsetTracker`) when `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` (`self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` in `__init__`), and `create_with_partitions` reuses that same pool across strategy instances. `OffsetTracker` has no API to drop/clear per-partition state on partition revocation/rebalance; it only trims offsets via `mark_committed` and never removes `outstanding` entries or partition keys. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:185 — Queues are unbounded and submit never raises MessageRejected, so there is no backpressure (the docstring says there is) and memory grows without limit when workers fall behind

adjudication.rationale: In FixedQueuePool.__init__ each work queue is created as queue.Queue() with no maxsize, so it is unbounded. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:234 — Shutdown sets worker.shutdown before the non-immediate queue shutdown, so workers drop queued items instead of draining them, the final commit runs before workers stop, and a worker still running after the 5s join timeout can overlap with the partition's new owner

adjudication.rationale: In FixedQueuePool.shutdown(), it sets each worker's `shutdown = True` before attempting `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` and joining. But OrderedQueueWorker.run() loops `while not self.shutdown:` and only calls `get()` inside that loop, so a worker that reaches the top of the loop after `shutdown` is set will exit immediately without draining already-queued WorkItems. Additionally, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() stops and joins the commit thread (`shutdown_event.set(); commit_thread.join(...)`) before calling `queue_pool.shutdown()`, so workers can still complete offsets after the commit loop has exited, leaving committable offsets uncommitted. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:185 — Per-group queues are unbounded queue.Queue() and submit() never raises MessageRejected, so there is no backpressure to Kafka and a slow result_processor lets the consumer buffer the whole backlog in memory (the docstring's "natural backpressure" claim is false).

adjudication.rationale: In FixedQueuePool.__init__ each per-group work queue is created as queue.Queue() with no maxsize (unbounded). FixedQueuePool.submit() always calls work_queue.put(work_item) and never raises a rejection/backpressure signal. As a result, if result_processor is slow, the consumer can continue ingesting and enqueue an arbitrarily large backlog in memory. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:59 — OffsetTracker.all_offsets/outstanding only get pruned up to the lowest contiguous completed offset, so one slow/stuck item, or a Kafka offset gap (transaction control records, compaction) that the range scan at line 89 treats as a break, blocks commits forever and makes the sets grow without bound.

adjudication.rationale: In OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets, committable progress per partition stops at the first offset that is either still outstanding or not present in all_offsets (the `else: break` in the range scan). Offsets are only pruned in mark_committed, which runs only when a committable offset is found; so if one offset never completes (or an offset is never added to all_offsets for any reason), no further commits happen and all subsequently seen offsets remain in all_offsets, causing unbounded growth of the tracking sets for that partition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:83 — get_committable_offsets does O(n) min()/max() over the full offset set every second while holding the partition lock that submit (add_offset) and every worker (complete_offset) need, so hot-path stalls grow with the backlog.

adjudication.rationale: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets`, the code acquires the per-partition lock and then computes `min(all_offsets)`, `max(all_offsets)`, and iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1)` while doing set membership checks (`offset in all_offsets` / `offset not in outstanding`). This work scales with the size/range of the backlog and is executed from the background commit thread every second (`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop`), while the same lock is also needed by the hot-path `add_offset` (submit) and `complete_offset` (every worker completion). That creates a concrete contention/perf risk grounded in the diff, but it’s not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:105 — mark_committed rebuilds the whole all_offsets set with a comprehension under the partition lock on every commit (O(n) allocation per partition per second) instead of pruning incrementally, and never prunes the outstanding set.

adjudication.rationale: In OffsetTracker.mark_committed (queue_consumer.py), the code rebuilds self.all_offsets[partition] with a set comprehension (`{o for o in ... if o > offset}`), which is an O(n) allocation under the per-partition lock each time a commit happens. The method also does not modify/prune `self.outstanding` at all. However, this is not a clear correctness bug from the diff because `get_committable_offsets` only returns offsets that are not in `outstanding`, and offsets are removed from `outstanding` via complete_offset in worker `finally` blocks and in error paths in submit(), so `outstanding` should not normally retain committed offsets. This is therefore a diff-grounded performance/housekeeping concern rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:312 — WorkItem keeps the full raw Kafka Message alongside the decoded result, but workers never read work_item.message, so each queued item holds the payload bytes twice in unbounded queues.

Since `FixedQueuePool` uses default `queue.Queue()` instances (unbounded), this change can unnecessarily retain the full raw Kafka payload/headers alongside the decoded `result`, increasing memory pressure without functional benefit. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:327 — poll() runs on every arroyo loop iteration and calls get_stats(), which locks and reads qsize() on all N queues and emits a gauge every time, adding avoidable per-poll overhead.

This design guarantees in-order processing per group, but it also means a hot `group_key` (or multiple keys mapping to the same queue index, including due to modulo collisions) will concentrate load onto one single-threaded worker while other workers may be underutilized. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:338 — Strategy close()/join() shuts down the factory-owned shared FixedQueuePool, so after any rebalance create_with_partitions reuses a pool with shut-down queues and dead workers; every later put() raises ShutDown, which submit() catches and marks complete, so all messages are silently dropped and their offsets committed.

adjudication.rationale: In `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, `self.queue_pool` is created once for mode `"thread-queue-parallel"` and then reused in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` for each `create_with_partitions` call. But `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` (and thus `join()`) calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which shuts down the underlying `queue.Queue` instances and worker threads. After a rebalance/new `create_with_partitions`, the factory will reuse the same (now shut down) `FixedQueuePool` (factory does not set `queue_pool=None` except in `factory.shutdown`). Subsequent `FixedQueuePool.submit()` will hit `work_queue.put(work_item)` on a shut down queue (raising `queue.ShutDown`), which is caught by `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` and then it marks the offset complete without processing, allowing the commit loop to commit offsets—silently dropping messages as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:287 — The arroyo Commit callback runs on a background daemon thread instead of inside submit/poll, which races StreamProcessor/KafkaConsumer state (buffered messages, staged offsets, revocation handling) that isn't thread-safe.

In `ResultsStrategyFactory.create_thread_queue_parallel_worker`, `commit_function` directly invokes the provided `commit` callback (`commit(commit_data)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:185 — The queues are unbounded (queue.Queue() with no maxsize) and submit never raises MessageRejected, so there is no backpressure (despite the docstring saying there is): slow processing causes unbounded memory growth, since each WorkItem holds the full Message.

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.__init__`, each `work_queue` is created as `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, making it unbounded. `FixedQueuePool.submit` always does `work_queue.put(work_item)` and never raises any rejection/backpressure signal. This directly contradicts the `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring claim of “Natural backpressure when queues fill up” and means slow processing can accumulate an unbounded number of `WorkItem`s. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:74 — OffsetTracker never drops revoked partitions, so completed-but-uncommitted offsets for a revoked partition stay committable forever; arroyo's stage_offsets rejects unassigned partitions for the whole dict, so every later commit fails (and the failure is only logged).

adjudication.rationale: The new OffsetTracker in `queue_consumer.py` retains per-Partition state indefinitely (`all_offsets`, `outstanding`, `last_committed`, `partition_locks`) and there is no mechanism in the diff to drop/reset state for partitions that are no longer active (e.g., after a rebalance). `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` always calls `commit_function(committable)` as a single dict and only logs exceptions; it does not filter partitions or recover by removing problematic partitions. While the claim about Arroyo rejecting unassigned partitions cannot be verified from this diff, the diff does show a real edge-case robustness gap: a single partition that causes commit to fail (including due to revocation) could cause repeated commit failures and prevent committing offsets for other partitions because the commit is attempted as an all-or-nothing dict and failed commits are retried forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:234 — shutdown() sets worker.shutdown=True before queue.shutdown(immediate=False), so workers exit after their current item and abandon queued items instead of draining them; those offsets stay outstanding in the shared tracker for good.

adjudication.rationale: In FixedQueuePool.shutdown(), it sets worker.shutdown = True before shutting down the queues. OrderedQueueWorker.run() exits its loop as soon as it finishes the current item (top-of-loop checks `while not self.shutdown`), so it will not drain any remaining queued WorkItem(s). Those queued items had their offsets added via OffsetTracker.add_offset() in submit(), but will never reach complete_offset(), leaving them permanently outstanding and preventing OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets() from advancing past them while the process is still running. This contradicts the method’s own “Gracefully shutdown” intent and can stall commits if shutdown is invoked while the strategy/commit loop is still active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:337 — close() stops the commit thread before draining the worker pool, so there is no final commit for work that finishes during shutdown, and that work is reprocessed after the rebalance.

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` the shutdown flow is: `shutdown_event.set()` → `commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)` → `queue_pool.shutdown()`. The commit loop `_commit_loop()` exits as soon as `shutdown_event` is set (`while not self.shutdown_event.is_set(): ...`), so it will not perform a final `get_committable_offsets()`/`commit_function()` after workers finish in-flight items during shutdown. Meanwhile, worker threads can still complete currently-processing items and call `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` in `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` after the commit thread has stopped. Those newly-committable offsets will never be committed, causing reprocessing after a rebalance/restart. The diff shows no drain-and-final-commit step (e.g., `wait_until_empty()` + final commit).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:243 — Workers are joined one at a time with a 5s timeout each (plus 5s for the commit thread), and join() ignores its timeout argument, so close() can block the rebalance callback for 100s+ with the default 20 queues.

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`, workers are joined in a loop with `worker.join(timeout=5.0)` for each worker, so with the default `num_queues=20` this can block up to ~100s just on worker joins, plus `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` also does `self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)` before calling `queue_pool.shutdown()`. Additionally, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(self, timeout: float | None = None)` ignores the `timeout` argument and always calls `self.close()`, so callers cannot bound shutdown time. This behavior is directly present in the diff and can realistically stall shutdown/rebalance handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:317 — submit()'s catch-all marks any failed enqueue or grouping as completed, turning infrastructure failures into silently committed message loss instead of surfacing the error or retrying.

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` the catch-all `except Exception:` logs the error and then (when `message.value` is a `BrokerValue`) calls `offset_tracker.add_offset(...)` immediately followed by `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)`. This marks the offset as processed even though decode/grouping/enqueue failed, allowing `_commit_loop()` to treat it as committable and call `commit_function(...)`, effectively skipping the failed message (data loss) rather than surfacing/retrying the failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:92 — The committable scan stops at the first offset not in all_offsets, so any gap in Kafka offsets (transaction markers, compaction, skipped messages) permanently stalls commits for that partition.

adjudication.rationale: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets`, the loop iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1)` and breaks unless `offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding`. That means if `all_offsets` contains a non-contiguous set (e.g. offsets 100 and 102 were added, but 101 was never added), the scan hits 101 (`offset not in all_offsets`) and breaks, preventing commits past 100. If such a gap never appears in `all_offsets`, commits for that partition cannot advance beyond the gap, effectively stalling commits despite later offsets being processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:129 — Nothing checks whether worker threads are alive: if a worker dies (e.g. a BaseException, or an error from metrics in the finally block), its queue grows forever and its offsets never complete, silently freezing commits for the affected partitions.

adjudication.rationale: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, the `finally` block calls `metrics.gauge(...)` without any exception handling. If `metrics.gauge` (or `offset_tracker.complete_offset`) raises, that exception will escape `run` and terminate the thread. `BaseException` from `result_processor` is also not caught (only `Exception`). `FixedQueuePool.submit`/`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` never checks `worker.is_alive()` or respawns workers, so a dead worker leaves its queue un-drained while offsets remain in `OffsetTracker.outstanding`, causing `get_committable_offsets()` to stop advancing and commits to stall indefinitely for affected partitions. This failure mode is visible from the diff and matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:340 — terminate() never joins the commit thread, which can still call commit() on a closing or closed consumer after terminate returns.

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__`, a daemon `commit_thread` is started to run `_commit_loop`, which can call `self.commit_function(committable)`. `close()` sets `shutdown_event` and then `join()`s the commit thread, but `terminate()` only sets `shutdown_event` and shuts down the queue pool without joining the commit thread. Since `_commit_loop` wakes up on a 1s wait and may already be mid-iteration when `terminate()` is called, it can still call `commit_function` after `terminate()` returns, potentially committing on a closing/closed consumer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:291 — Commit-loop failures are only logged, with no metric or escalation, so a commit path that keeps failing goes unnoticed while lag grows.

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` (around the reported line), any exception—including repeated commit failures—is caught and only `logger.exception("Error in commit loop")` is emitted. There is no `metrics.incr`/gauge for commit-loop errors and no other escalation/backoff behavior. This is an observability/operational gap introduced with the new commit thread: if commits keep failing, processing continues but offsets won’t advance and lag can grow without a metric signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:238 — Queue.shutdown and queue.ShutDown need Python 3.13+; on older runtimes shutdown() fails with a logged AttributeError, and workers blocked in get() never exit.

adjudication.rationale: The new implementation explicitly relies on `queue.Queue.shutdown(...)` and the `queue.ShutDown` exception in multiple places (e.g., `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` catches `queue.ShutDown` around `self.work_queue.get()`, and `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`). If the project runtime does not provide these APIs, shutdown will raise (caught and logged in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`), and worker threads blocked in `get()` will not be released, causing hangs/leaks on shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1922 — test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts no commit happened, which contradicts the implementation (the worker's `finally` completes and commits failed offsets) and only passes because the test finishes before the 1s commit-loop tick, so on a slow run it fails with {partition: 102}

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `OrderedQueueWorker.run` always calls `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` in `finally`, even if `result_processor(...)` raises (it only logs the exception). Then `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` periodically commits whatever `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets()` returns, and `ResultsStrategyFactory.create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` converts those to Kafka commits with `offset + 1`. Therefore a failed message is still marked complete and can advance committable/committed offsets (e.g., offsets 100 and 101 both “complete” => commit 101+1=102). The test `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` asserting no commit for that partition can indeed be timing-dependent because `_commit_loop` ticks every ~1s (`wait(1.0)`), so on slower runs it may commit `{partition: 102}` and fail. adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1979 — test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps breaks out 0.2s after the first commit, before the second tick, and so misses that OffsetTracker commits 103 (104) on the next tick: after mark_committed prunes, start=max(last_committed+1, min_offset) at queue_consumer.py:86 jumps over the gap

adjudication.rationale: The new OffsetTracker can incorrectly allow committing past an offset gap after mark_committed prunes old offsets. With offsets {100,102,103}: first get_committable_offsets commits 100, then mark_committed prunes all_offsets to {102,103}. Next get_committable_offsets computes start=max(last_committed+1, min_offset)=max(101,102)=102 and will treat 102 and 103 as contiguous, returning committable=103, effectively skipping missing 101. This behavior is present in queue_consumer.py (get_committable_offsets start calculation + mark_committed pruning). The cited test in test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps breaks shortly after the first commit and likely won’t observe the second commit tick (commit loop is 1s), so it can miss this defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:338 — No test covers rebalance (close/join and then create_with_partitions again). strategy.close() shuts down the factory-owned shared FixedQueuePool, so the next strategy's put() raises ShutDown, which submit() catches and marks complete, silently dropping messages; OffsetTracker state for revoked partitions is also never cleared

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates and owns a single `FixedQueuePool` in `__init__` when `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` and then reuses it in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` (`assert self.queue_pool is not None`). If the factory later creates a new strategy (e.g., after close/join on rebalance), it will reuse the same (now-shutdown) pool, and `FixedQueuePool.submit()` will call `work_queue.put(work_item)` on a shutdown queue, which can raise `queue.ShutDown`. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` catches broad `Exception` and marks the offset complete, effectively dropping the message while allowing offsets to advance (data loss). adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py:372 — The second phase of test_offset_gaps_block_commits passes vacuously: 103 is committed on the next tick whether or not 101 is submitted, because the gap is skipped after mark_committed, and no OffsetTracker unit test covers the gap-after-commit case

adjudication.rationale: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets`, the computation `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)` (queue_consumer.py) allows the tracker to “skip” missing offsets that were never added to `all_offsets`. After `mark_committed(100)` removes `<=100`, `all_offsets` can become `{102, 103}`, making `min_offset=102` and enabling a later commit of `103` even if `101` was never submitted. That means in `test_offset_gaps_block_commits` (test_queue_consumer.py: second phase), the asserted commit to `103` can occur on the next commit-loop tick regardless of submitting `101`, so the second phase does not necessarily validate the intended gap behavior. adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py:312 — test_preserves_order_within_group only asserts len==5 and never checks processing order, even though ordering is what its name says it tests

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py:415 — The strategy created by create_with_partitions is never closed, so its commit thread (daemon, shutdown_event never set) keeps looping after the test ends; the same leak happens in every thread-queue test in test_results_consumer.py (e.g. line 1695), and factory.shutdown() is not in try/finally

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:335 — No test checks close()/join() draining: close stops the commit thread without a final commit and then shuts down the queues, so offsets processed since the last tick are never committed, and no test asserts that workers exit or that pending items get processed

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:2005 — test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown only asserts queue_pool is None; the real processor runs on worker threads outside the feature override and test DB transaction, and nothing verifies the 5 submitted messages were processed, that the workers stopped, or that offsets were committed

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py:200 — assert stats["total_items"] > 0` right after submit is timing-dependent: the workers can drain the queues (qsize drops on get) before get_stats runs

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py:106 — test_different_groups_distributed depends on per-process randomized str hash() to spread 20 keys over 3 queues, so it is slightly nondeterministic, and nothing tests that assignment is stable across processes/restarts

The test `test_different_groups_distributed` collects `hash(f"group{i}") % 3` for i=0..19 and asserts `len(queue_indices) == 3`, which is probabilistic (it can, in principle, hit only 1–2 buckets depending on the salted hash) and therefore slightly nondeterministic/flaky. Also, nothing in the tests checks cross-process/restart stability, and with `hash()` it would not be stable anyway.
